where: Section 2, the paragraph beginning "Locating test items is the mapping step"
problem: The paragraph mixes up test items with requirements. A test item is the thing being tested (a build, module, interface or document, identified by name and version). The mapping that the plan records is between requirements and test cases, not between test items and requirements. A student will carry this confusion into the RTM described in Section 3, where rows are requirements, not test items.
fix: "Test items are the builds, modules, interfaces and documents that will actually be tested; each is named and versioned so the tester knows exactly what is under test. The mapping step is the requirement-to-test-case trace kept in the RTM: each feature to be tested is linked forward to the test cases that exercise it and backward to the requirement that asked for it."

problem: The example treats the 40 automated cases as costing nothing: each full cycle is charged only for the 95 manual cases, and the two testers are assumed to work in perfect parallel. Re-running automated suites, checking their results and maintaining them takes real effort, so the 17.9-day answer is optimistic and the example does not say so.
fix: Keep the arithmetic, but state the assumption in step 7 and record it as a risk: "Assumes automated cases need no manual effort per cycle and that the two testers work fully in parallel. If either fails, the 18-day window is missed."
